issues.title: Single underscore include guard used
issues.description: The rule requires header files to use include guards with double underscores at the start (e.g., __FILENAME_H), but the code uses a single underscore prefix instead (_REDIS_H)
issues.rule_name: Header Files Must Use Double-Underscore Include Guards

issues.title: Unsigned integer wraparound in AOF corruption size check
issues.description: The size comparison casts both operands to size_t (unsigned), which causes undefined behavior when valid_up_to exceeds sb.st_size. In this edge case, the subtraction sb.st_size - valid_up_to produces a negative value that wraps around to a very large unsigned integer, always exceeding aof_load_broken_max_size. This prevents automatic recovery even when the corruption is actually small, causing the server to fail to start when it should recover successfully.

issues.title: Incorrect early exit prevents loading incremental AOF after successful base recovery
issues.description: The error handling condition incorrectly treats AOF_BROKEN_RECOVERED as a failure state, causing the function to exit immediately after successfully recovering a corrupted base AOF file. When a base AOF is the last file and gets successfully recovered (ret == AOF_BROKEN_RECOVERED), the server should continue to load any incremental AOF files. However, this bug causes an early exit to cleanup, preventing incremental files from being loaded and potentially losing data. The correct behavior is to only exit on AOF_OPEN_ERR or AOF_FAILED, not on successful recovery.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #14058 - Add auto-repair options for broken AOF tail on startup

structured_output.summary:
This PR adds two configs, `aof-load-broken` and `aof-load-broken-max-size`. When the AOF loader hits a format error (`fmterr`) and the corrupted tail is smaller than the threshold, Redis truncates the file at the last well-formed command and keeps starting up. It also adds a new `AOF_BROKEN_RECOVERED` return code, which `loadAppendOnlyFiles` treats like `AOF_TRUNCATED` when deciding whether a file is the last one.

The idea is useful, but the integration has real problems. First, the base-file branch now jumps to `cleanup` on `AOF_BROKEN_RECOVERED`. That skips setting `aof_current_size` and `aof_rewrite_base_size`, so INFO shows the wrong sizes and auto-rewrite fires at the wrong time. Second, `stopLoading()` doesn't count `AOF_BROKEN_RECOVERED` as success, so modules get a LOADING_FAILED event even after a successful recovery. Third, the `fmterr` path ignores the MULTI/EXEC rollback that the EOF path uses. It can leave a dangling `MULTI` at the end of the file, and on the next restart every write appended after it gets reverted. Finally, the file is truncated on disk before the caller checks whether it's the last file. A broken intermediate file gets cut down and the server exits, then the next boot loads cleanly with a silent gap in the history.
structured_output.verdictRationale: I'm requesting changes because of four confirmed bugs. After a base-only recovery the size counters are never set. Module loading events are wrong. The MULTI-aware truncation is missing, which can lose data on the next restart. And files that aren't last are truncated on disk before startup is aborted. All four are on the recovery path this PR adds.

architecture.overview:
On startup, `loadDataFromDisk` calls `loadAppendOnlyFiles`, which reads the manifest and calls `loadSingleAppendOnlyFile` for the BASE file and then each INCR file. While replaying commands, the single-file loader tracks `valid_up_to`, the offset after the last fully executed command. Before this PR, only an unexpected EOF (`uxeof`) could be repaired, and only when `aof-load-truncated` was on. That repair truncates to `valid_up_to`, or to `valid_before_multi` if the file stopped inside a MULTI block, and returns `AOF_TRUNCATED`. The multi-file loader accepts that result only for the last file.

This PR adds a matching repair for format errors (`fmterr`), controlled by `aof-load-broken`. If the gap between the file size and `valid_up_to` is below `aof-load-broken-max-size`, the file is truncated to `valid_up_to` and `AOF_BROKEN_RECOVERED` is returned. The multi-file loader treats the new code like `AOF_TRUNCATED` for the last-file check. In the base-file branch it also jumps straight to `cleanup`, and `stopLoading` still counts only `AOF_OK`/`AOF_TRUNCATED` as success.
steps: Start at `loadDataFromDisk` (src/server.c:7033). It only exits on `AOF_FAILED`/`AOF_OPEN_ERR`, so any other code, including the new `AOF_BROKEN_RECOVERED`, means startup continues.

`loadAppendOnlyFiles` (src/aof.c:1773) loads the BASE file and then the INCR files. It turns a TRUNCATED or BROKEN_RECOVERED result into FAILED when the file isn't last, and it initializes `aof_current_size`/`aof_rewrite_base_size` after the loop.
`loadSingleAppendOnlyFile` replays commands and updates `valid_up_to` after each one. That update now also runs when `aof_load_broken` is on (line 1661).
The new `fmterr` branch (lines 1721-1756) compares `sb.st_size - valid_up_to` against `aof_load_broken_max_size`, truncates the file on disk, and jumps to `loaded_ok` with `AOF_BROKEN_RECOVERED`.
Compare it with the existing `uxeof` branch and the MULTI handling at lines 1667-1675: that path rewinds to `valid_before_multi`, while the new `fmterr` path doesn't.
The new configs are registered in src/config.c and documented in redis.conf. Tests in tests/integration/aof.tcl cover base, incr, intermediate-file and over-threshold cases.

findings.title: Base-only recovery skips aof_current_size / aof_rewrite_base_size initialization
findings.fixPrompt: In src/aof.c, loadAppendOnlyFiles(), the base-file branch (around line 1841) jumps to `cleanup` when `ret == AOF_BROKEN_RECOVERED`. When the base file is the last file and was recovered, this skips the initialization of `server.aof_current_size` and `server.aof_rewrite_base_size` after the INCR loop. Remove `|| ret == AOF_BROKEN_RECOVERED` from that condition so it matches the INCR loop (`AOF_OPEN_ERR || AOF_FAILED` only). Extend the 'Corrupted base AOF (last file)' test in tests/integration/aof.tcl to assert that `aof_current_size` in INFO persistence is non-zero.

findings.title: fmterr truncation ignores MULTI state, leaving a dangling MULTI that can revert future writes
findings.fixPrompt: In src/aof.c, loadSingleAppendOnlyFile(), the new fmterr recovery branch (around lines 1724-1756) truncates the AOF at `valid_up_to` even when the fake client is inside a MULTI block (`fakeClient->flags & CLIENT_MULTI`). That leaves an unclosed MULTI at the end of the file, and on the next restart it swallows or reverts newly appended writes. Before computing the broken size and truncating, check for CLIENT_MULTI; if set, log a warning and set `valid_up_to = valid_before_multi`, the same way the EOF path does at lines 1667-1675. Add a test in tests/integration/aof.tcl: AOF with `multi`, `set a 1`, then 'corruption'; start with aof-load-broken yes, write a key, restart, and assert the key survives.

findings.title: Intermediate files are truncated on disk before the 'not last file' fatal check, so the next boot silently loses data
findings.body:
The truncation happens inside `loadSingleAppendOnlyFile`. Whether the file is the last one is only checked later, in `loadAppendOnlyFiles`:

::diff{file="src/aof.c" lines="1868-1873"}

When a BASE or middle INCR file has a format error, this PR has already cut it down on disk by the time Redis logs "Fatal error: the truncated file is not the last file" and exits. On the next restart the file parses cleanly, the check passes, and Redis applies the later INCR files on top of a history with the dropped commands missing. That silent gap is exactly what the "not the last file" check is meant to prevent.

The new tests run into this: "Log should mention truncated file is not last" and "Intermediate AOF is broken" both truncate the file and then expect a fatal exit, but neither restarts again to see what happens next. (`aof-load-truncated` has the same ordering issue, but before this PR a format error never modified the file.)

A cleaner design is to pass a `last_file` flag (or a "may truncate" flag) into `loadSingleAppendOnlyFile` and only truncate when the file is last. Otherwise, fail without touching the file.
findings.fixPrompt: In src/aof.c, loadSingleAppendOnlyFile() truncates the AOF on disk in the new fmterr recovery branch (lines ~1724-1746) before loadAppendOnlyFiles() checks whether the file is the last one (lines ~1836 and ~1870). As a result, a corrupted BASE or middle INCR file is shortened, startup fails, and the next restart succeeds with missing history. Change loadSingleAppendOnlyFile to take a parameter saying whether truncation is allowed (i.e., this is the last file), and only run the fmterr truncate/recover path when it is; otherwise return AOF_FAILED without modifying the file. Update both callers in loadAppendOnlyFiles and the DEBUG/old-style call sites. Extend the 'Intermediate AOF is broken' test in tests/integration/aof.tcl to restart a second time and assert the server still refuses to start.

findings.title: stopLoading reports failure to modules after a successful broken-tail recovery
findings.fixPrompt: In src/aof.c at the end of loadAppendOnlyFiles() (around line 1894), `stopLoading(ret == AOF_OK || ret == AOF_TRUNCATED)` doesn't count the new `AOF_BROKEN_RECOVERED` code as success, so modules receive REDISMODULE_SUBEVENT_LOADING_FAILED after a successful recovery. Add `|| ret == AOF_BROKEN_RECOVERED` to that expression. Also update the doc comment above loadSingleAppendOnlyFile (line ~1477) and the `loaded_ok` label comment to mention AOF_BROKEN_RECOVERED.

findings.title: A small RDB-encoded base file with trailing garbage is truncated to zero bytes
findings.body:
`valid_up_to` starts at 0, and nothing updates it after the RDB preamble or RDB base file finishes loading (lines 1530-1554). If an RDB-format base file has garbage after the RDB EOF marker and no AOF commands run successfully before the error, `fmterr` sees `sb.st_size - 0` as the "broken size". For files under 4KB, which is the default threshold, it truncates the **whole file**, including the valid RDB data that was just loaded into memory.

::diff{file="src/aof.c" lines="1724-1730"}

The reported "broken size" is also misleading: it counts the RDB section as corruption. The `valid_up_to == -1` check never fires in this case because the value is 0, not -1.

Setting `valid_up_to = ftello(fp)` after a successful `rdbLoadRio` fixes this and makes the size calculation correct.
findings.fixPrompt: In src/aof.c, loadSingleAppendOnlyFile(), after a successful rdbLoadRio() in the RDB-preamble branch (around lines 1548-1553), `valid_up_to` stays 0. If a format error follows the RDB section, the new fmterr recovery (lines ~1724-1746) computes the broken size as the whole file and may truncate the file to 0 bytes, deleting valid RDB data. After the RDB load succeeds, set `valid_up_to = ftello(fp)` (and `valid_before_multi` to the same value). Add a test with an RDB-format base plus appended garbage and aof-load-broken yes, and assert that the base file isn't emptied.

findings.title: Unrelated include-guard rename in server.h
findings.body:
The guard was changed from `__REDIS_H` to `_REDIS_H`. It doesn't break anything, since the `#endif` has no named comment, but it has nothing to do with AOF recovery and adds noise to the diff and to downstream merges. Please revert it or move it to a separate PR.

::diff{file="src/server.h" lines="15-16"}
findings.fixPrompt: In src/server.h lines 15-16, the include guard was renamed from `__REDIS_H` to `_REDIS_H`, which is unrelated to this PR's AOF recovery feature. Revert it to `__REDIS_H`.

findings.title: Opt-in default and size cap are a sensible safety design
findings.body:
Shipping `aof-load-broken no` by default, with a small byte cap (`4096`), keeps the risk of automatic truncation bounded and opt-in. The redis.conf text clearly states the availability-versus-integrity trade-off. The log messages for the recovered and over-limit cases include both the broken size and the threshold, which helps operators.

::code{file="redis.conf" lines="1532-1549"}
